CHAPTER 7 — अयोध्यां प्रत्यागमनम् (AYODHYAM PRATYAGAMANAM)

Introduction — प्रस्तावना

अयोध्यां प्रत्यागमनम् means "the return to Ayodhya". This lesson retells, in simple correct Sanskrit prose, the joyful close of the great epic रामायणम् (Ramayana) composed by महर्षि वाल्मीकि (the sage Valmiki): the day श्रीरामः (Sri Rama) came home to अयोध्या (Ayodhya) after चतुर्दश वर्षाणि (fourteen years) of वनवासः (forest-exile). It is one of the most beloved episodes of Indian tradition, celebrated even today as दीपावली (Deepavali), the festival of lamps, when people light rows of lamps to welcome Rama home. Here we read the story (कथा) in easy Sanskrit with word-meanings (शब्दार्थ) and an English translation, draw out its moral (सन्देशः), study three or four famous public-domain verses (श्लोकाः) in praise of Rama, and learn a little grammar (व्याकरणम्) — सन्धि, विभक्ति, शब्दरूप and धातुरूप — from the words of the lesson.

The background — कथायाः पृष्ठभूमिः

श्रीरामः अयोध्यायाः राजा दशरथस्य ज्येष्ठः पुत्रः आसीत्। (Sri Rama was the eldest son of Dasharatha, the king of Ayodhya.) पितुः वचनं पालयितुं सः चतुर्दश वर्षाणि वनम् अगच्छत्। (To keep his father's word, he went to the forest for fourteen years.) तेन सह पत्नी सीता भ्राता च लक्ष्मणः अपि वनम् अगच्छताम्। (With him his wife Sita and his brother Lakshmana also went to the forest.) वने रावणः नाम राक्षसः सीताम् अहरत्। (In the forest a demon named Ravana carried off Sita.) रामः वानराणां सहायेन लङ्कां गत्वा रावणं युद्धे अहन्। (With the help of the monkeys (vanaras), Rama went to Lanka and killed Ravana in battle.) एवं सीता मुक्ता अभवत्। (Thus Sita was freed.)

शब्दार्थ: राजा = king; ज्येष्ठः = eldest; पुत्रः = son; पितुः = of the father; वचनम् = word/promise; पालयितुम् = in order to keep/obey; वर्षाणि = years; वनम् = forest; पत्नी = wife; भ्राता = brother; राक्षसः = demon; अहरत् = carried off; वानराणाम् = of the monkeys; सहायेन = with the help; युद्धे = in battle; अहन् = killed; मुक्ता = freed.

The homecoming — प्रत्यागमनम्

रावणस्य वधानन्तरं रामः सीतया लक्ष्मणेन च सह अयोध्यां प्रत्यागन्तुम् ऐच्छत्। (After the killing of Ravana, Rama wished to return to Ayodhya with Sita and Lakshmana.) विभीषणः रामाय पुष्पकं नाम विमानम् अयच्छत्। (Vibhishana gave Rama the aerial car named Pushpaka.) तेन विमानेन रामः सुग्रीवेण हनूमता विभीषणेन वानरैः च सह आकाशमार्गेण प्रस्थितः। (By that vehicle Rama set out by the sky-path together with Sugriva, Hanuman, Vibhishana and the monkeys.) मार्गे ते प्रयागे भरद्वाजस्य आश्रमम् अगच्छन्। (On the way they went to the hermitage of Bharadwaja at Prayaga.) ऋषिः तान् सस्नेहम् अपूजयत्। (The sage honoured them with affection.)

ततः रामः हनूमन्तम् अब्रवीत् — "गच्छ, भरतं मम आगमनस्य वार्तां कथय।" (Then Rama said to Hanuman — "Go, tell Bharata the news of my coming.") हनूमान् शीघ्रं नन्दिग्रामं गत्वा भरताय शुभं समाचारम् अकथयत्। (Hanuman quickly went to Nandigrama and told Bharata the good news.) भरतः चतुर्दश वर्षाणि रामस्य पादुके सिंहासने स्थापयित्वा तापसवेषेण राज्यम् अपालयत्। (For fourteen years Bharata, having placed Rama's sandals upon the throne, ruled the kingdom in the garb of an ascetic.) समाचारं श्रुत्वा भरतस्य नेत्रे आनन्दाश्रुभिः पूर्णे अभवताम्। (Hearing the news, Bharata's two eyes filled with tears of joy.)

शब्दार्थ: वधानन्तरम् = after the killing; प्रत्यागन्तुम् = to return; ऐच्छत् = wished; विमानम् = aerial car; अयच्छत् = gave; आकाशमार्गेण = by the sky-path; प्रस्थितः = set out; आश्रमम् = hermitage; ऋषिः = sage; अपूजयत् = honoured; अब्रवीत् = said; वार्ताम्/समाचारम् = news; शीघ्रम् = quickly; पादुके = the pair of sandals; सिंहासने = on the throne; स्थापयित्वा = having placed; तापसवेषेण = in ascetic's dress; अपालयत् = ruled/protected; नेत्रे = the two eyes; आनन्दाश्रुभिः = with tears of joy; पूर्णे = filled.

The reunion and the coronation — मिलनम् राज्याभिषेकः च

रामे अयोध्यां प्रविष्टे सति सर्वे नागरिकाः अतीव प्रसन्नाः अभवन्। (When Rama entered Ayodhya, all the citizens became very happy.) जनाः गृहाणि दीपैः पुष्पैः तोरणैः च अशोभयन्। (The people adorned their houses with lamps, flowers and festoons.) माता कौसल्या पुत्रं दृष्ट्वा हर्षेण अरोदीत्। (Mother Kausalya, seeing her son, wept with joy.) भरतः भ्रातरं रामं प्रणम्य पादुके तस्मै अर्पयत्। (Bharata, bowing to his brother Rama, gave back to him the sandals.)

अनन्तरं गुरुः वसिष्ठः शुभे मुहूर्ते रामस्य राज्याभिषेकम् अकरोत्। (Then the preceptor Vasishtha performed Rama's coronation at an auspicious moment.) रामः अयोध्यायाः राजा अभवत्। (Rama became the king of Ayodhya.) तस्य शासने प्रजाः धर्मेण जीवन्ति स्म, सर्वे च सुखिनः निरामयाः च आसन्। (Under his rule the subjects lived by righteousness, and all were happy and free from disease.) एतत् आदर्शराज्यं "रामराज्यम्" इति प्रसिद्धम्। (This ideal kingdom is famous as "Rama-rajya".)

शब्दार्थ: प्रविष्टे = having entered; नागरिकाः = citizens; अतीव = very much; अशोभयन् = decorated; दीपैः = with lamps; तोरणैः = with festoons/arches; हर्षेण = with joy; अरोदीत् = wept; प्रणम्य = having bowed; अर्पयत् = offered/gave back; गुरुः = teacher/preceptor; मुहूर्ते = at the (auspicious) moment; राज्याभिषेकम् = coronation; शासने = under the rule; प्रजाः = subjects/people; धर्मेण = by righteousness; निरामयाः = free from disease; आदर्शराज्यम् = ideal kingdom; प्रसिद्धम् = famous.

English translation (सम्पूर्ण-अनुवादः)

Sri Rama, the eldest son of King Dasharatha of Ayodhya, went to the forest for fourteen years to honour his father's promise. His wife Sita and his brother Lakshmana went with him. In the forest the demon Ravana carried off Sita; with the help of the vanaras, Rama went to Lanka, killed Ravana in battle, and freed Sita. After the war Rama wished to return home. Vibhishana gave him the flying chariot Pushpaka, and Rama set out through the sky with Sugriva, Hanuman, Vibhishana and the monkeys. On the way he visited the hermitage of the sage Bharadwaja, who welcomed them warmly. Rama then sent Hanuman ahead to carry the good news to Bharata, who for fourteen years had placed Rama's sandals on the throne and ruled Ayodhya as a humble ascetic in Rama's name. Overjoyed, Bharata went out to meet him. When Rama entered Ayodhya the whole city rejoiced, lighting lamps and hanging garlands. Mother Kausalya wept with happiness; Bharata bowed and returned the sandals. The sage Vasishtha crowned Rama king at an auspicious hour, and under Rama's righteous rule — Rama-rajya — all the people lived happily, honestly and without suffering.

सन्देशः (Moral)

The chapter teaches कर्तव्यपालनम् (doing one's duty), भ्रातृप्रेम (brotherly love) and धर्मराज्यम् (righteous rule). Rama kept his father's word even at great cost; Bharata ruled selflessly, holding the throne only in trust for his brother; and as king Rama placed the welfare of the people above his own comfort. The joy of the homecoming reminds us that truth (सत्यम्), sacrifice (त्यागः) and love finally lead to happiness. Rama-rajya remains India's timeless symbol of just and compassionate governance.

पद्यानि — Verses in praise of श्रीराम (with word-meanings)

1) रामाय रामभद्राय रामचन्द्राय वेधसे ।
   रघुनाथाय नाथाय सीतायाः पतये नमः ॥ (रामरक्षास्तोत्रम्)
   शब्दार्थ: रामाय = to Rama; रामभद्राय = to the auspicious Rama; रामचन्द्राय = to Rama-chandra (moon-like Rama); वेधसे = to the creator/wise one; रघुनाथाय = to the lord of the Raghus; नाथाय = to the lord/protector; सीतायाः = of Sita; पतये = to the husband; नमः = salutation.
   Translation: Salutation to Rama, to the gracious Rama, to Ramachandra, to the all-knowing one; salutation to the Lord of the Raghu dynasty, the protector, the husband of Sita.
   Note: Observe how "राम" here takes the चतुर्थी (dative, "to") ending -आय again and again — a beautiful model for learning case-forms.

2) राम राजमणिः सदा विजयते रामं रमेशं भजे
   रामेणाभिहता निशाचरचमू रामाय तस्मै नमः ।
   रामान्नास्ति परायणं परतरं रामस्य दासोऽस्म्यहम्
   रामे चित्तलयः सदा भवतु मे भो राम मामुद्धर ॥
   शब्दार्थ: राजमणिः = the jewel among kings (प्रथमा, nominative); रामम् = Rama (द्वितीया, object); रामेण = by Rama (तृतीया); रामाय = to Rama (चतुर्थी); रामात् = than/from Rama (पञ्चमी); रामस्य = of Rama (षष्ठी); रामे = in Rama (सप्तमी); राम/भो राम = O Rama (सम्बोधन, vocative); अभिहता = struck down; निशाचरचमू = the army of night-rangers (demons); परायणम् = refuge; दासः = servant; चित्तलयः = absorption of the mind; उद्धर = uplift/save.
   Translation: Rama the jewel of kings is ever victorious; I worship Rama the lord of Rama (Lakshmi); by Rama the demon army was struck down; to that Rama my salutation. There is no higher refuge than Rama; I am the servant of Rama; may my mind ever be absorbed in Rama; O Rama, uplift me.
   Note: This single famous verse displays the word "राम" in all eight cases (विभक्तयः) — the perfect verse for learning शब्दरूप.

3) रामो विग्रहवान् धर्मः साधुः सत्यपराक्रमः ।
   राजा सर्वस्य लोकस्य देवानामिव वासवः ॥ (वाल्मीकिरामायणम्)
   शब्दार्थ: विग्रहवान् = embodied, having a form; धर्मः = righteousness; साधुः = virtuous/noble; सत्यपराक्रमः = of true valour; राजा = king; सर्वस्य लोकस्य = of the whole world; देवानाम् = of the gods; इव = like; वासवः = Indra.
   Translation: Rama is righteousness personified, noble and of true valour; he is (fit to be) the king of the whole world, as Indra is (king) of the gods.
   Moral: Rama is dharma in human form — the very reason his return and rule bring joy to all.

4) आपदामपहर्तारं दातारं सर्वसम्पदाम् ।
   लोकाभिरामं श्रीरामं भूयो भूयो नमाम्यहम् ॥ (रामरक्षास्तोत्रम्)
   शब्दार्थ: आपदाम् = of calamities; अपहर्तारम् = the remover; दातारम् = the giver; सर्वसम्पदाम् = of all prosperity; लोकाभिरामम् = delighting the world; श्रीरामम् = Sri Rama; भूयो भूयः = again and again; नमामि = I bow; अहम् = I.
   Translation: Him who removes all calamities, the giver of every prosperity, Sri Rama who delights the world — again and again I bow to him.

व्याकरणम् — Grammar from the lesson

(A) सन्धि (Sandhi — the joining of sounds). Splitting a joined form (सन्धि-विच्छेदः) is a key reading skill.
  • राज्याभिषेकः = राज्य + अभिषेकः (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घ-सन्धि) — "coronation".
  • प्रत्यागमनम् = प्रति + आगमनम् (इ + आ = य् + आ, यण्-सन्धि) — "return".
  • रामायणम् = राम + अयनम् (अ + अ = आ) — "the journey/way of Rama".
  • वधानन्तरम् = वध + अनन्तरम् (अ + अ = आ) — "after the killing".
  • रामो विग्रहवान् = रामः + विग्रहवान् (visarga + व → ओ; विसर्ग-सन्धि).
  • रामान्नास्ति = रामात् + न + अस्ति (त् + न = न्न, व्यञ्जन-सन्धि; न + अस्ति = नास्ति).
  • मामुद्धर = माम् + उद्धर.

(B) विभक्ति (Vibhakti — case endings). Sanskrit nouns change ending to show their role. Using masculine a-stem राम:
  • प्रथमा (nominative, subject): रामः — "Rama (does)". In the lesson रामः अयोध्यां प्रत्यागच्छत्.
  • द्वितीया (accusative, object): रामम् — "(I worship) Rama". अयोध्याम्, सीताम्, रावणम् are objects.
  • तृतीया (instrumental, "by/with"): रामेण — "by Rama". सहायेन "with help", विमानेन "by the vehicle".
  • चतुर्थी (dative, "to/for"): रामाय — "to Rama". भरताय "to Bharata", रामाय नमः.
  • पञ्चमी (ablative, "from/than"): रामात् — "from/than Rama".
  • षष्ठी (genitive, "of"): रामस्य — "of Rama". दशरथस्य, रावणस्य.
  • सप्तमी (locative, "in/at/on"): रामे — "in Rama". वने "in the forest", सिंहासने "on the throne", मार्गे "on the way".
  • सम्बोधन (vocative, "O"): (हे) राम — "O Rama". भो राम मामुद्धर.

(C) शब्दरूप (declension of राम, masculine a-stem):
  प्रथमा: रामः / रामौ / रामाः; द्वितीया: रामम् / रामौ / रामान्; तृतीया: रामेण / रामाभ्याम् / रामैः;
  चतुर्थी: रामाय / रामाभ्याम् / रामेभ्यः; पञ्चमी: रामात् / रामाभ्याम् / रामेभ्यः;
  षष्ठी: रामस्य / रामयोः / रामाणाम्; सप्तमी: रामे / रामयोः / रामेषु; सम्बोधन: (हे) राम / रामौ / रामाः.

(D) धातुरूप (conjugation — present tense, लट् लकार). The verb गम् (to go, first class, becomes गच्छ-) in the present:
  एकवचन: गच्छति (he goes) / द्विवचन: गच्छतः / बहुवचन: गच्छन्ति;
  मध्यम-पुरुष: गच्छसि / गच्छथः / गच्छथ; उत्तम-पुरुष: गच्छामि / गच्छावः / गच्छामः.
  Note the past-tense (लङ् लकार) forms used in the story: अगच्छत् (he went), अभवत् (became), अपालयत् (ruled), अकरोत् (did/made).

SUMMARY (सारांश)

In this chapter you read, in simple Sanskrit, how श्रीरामः returned to अयोध्या after fourteen years of exile: the flight by the पुष्पकविमान, the visit to sage भरद्वाज, Hanuman's message to भरत, the reunion with भरत and माता कौसल्या, the giving-back of the पादुके, and the राज्याभिषेकः performed by वसिष्ठ that began the ideal रामराज्यम्. You learned the शब्दार्थ of each part, an English translation and the moral of duty, brotherly love and righteous rule. Four famous public-domain verses in praise of Rama gave you both devotional beauty and a natural way to learn grammar — especially the verse "राम राजमणिः..." which shows the word राम in all eight cases. Finally you studied सन्धि (and सन्धि-विच्छेदः), the eight विभक्ति endings, the शब्दरूप of राम, and the धातुरूप of गम्. Light a lamp, recite a verse, and remember: सत्यम् and धर्मः always lead home.

topics.description: The narrative of श्रीराम's return to अयोध्या after चतुर्दश वर्षाणि of exile: the victory over रावण, the flight by the पुष्पकविमान, the visit to भरद्वाज, and the arrival home — retold in simple Sanskrit.

topics.name: पात्राणि — Characters and the Homecoming
topics.description: The chief characters of the episode — राम, सीता, लक्ष्मण, भरत, हनुमान्, विभीषण, वसिष्ठ, कौसल्या — and their roles in the reunion, the return of the पादुके and the coronation.

topics.name: सन्देशः — Moral and Ethical Themes
topics.description: The values carried by the story — कर्तव्यपालनम् (duty), भ्रातृप्रेम (brotherly love), त्यागः (sacrifice), सत्यम् (truth) and धर्मराज्यम्/रामराज्यम् (righteous, compassionate governance).

chapter_summary.title: अयोध्यां प्रत्यागमनम् (Ayodhyam Pratyagamanam) — Chapter Summary
chapter_summary.intro: This is the NIOS Secondary Sanskrit (209) summary for Chapter 7. It retells, in simple Sanskrit, how श्रीराम returned to अयोध्या after fourteen years of exile, the joyful reunion and राज्याभिषेकः that began रामराज्यम्, presents famous public-domain verses in praise of Rama, and draws grammar — सन्धि, विभक्ति, शब्दरूप and धातुरूप — from the lesson.

sections.heading: The story of the return
bullets: After killing रावण and freeing सीता, राम wished to return home to अयोध्या.
विभीषण gave the पुष्पकविमान; राम flew back with सीता, लक्ष्मण, हनुमान्, सुग्रीव and the वानराः.
On the way they rested at the hermitage of the sage भरद्वाज at Prayaga.
The homecoming is celebrated as दीपावली, the festival of lamps.

sections.heading: The reunion and coronation
bullets: राम sent हनुमान् ahead to carry the good news to भरत at नन्दिग्राम.
भरत had ruled for fourteen years with राम's पादुके on the throne, as a humble ascetic.
भरत returned the sandals; माता कौसल्या wept with joy at seeing her son.
The preceptor वसिष्ठ performed राम's राज्याभिषेकः at an auspicious hour.

sections.heading: Themes and moral
bullets: राम kept his father's promise — कर्तव्यपालनम् and सत्यम् (truth).
भरत's selfless regency shows भ्रातृप्रेम (brotherly love) and त्यागः (sacrifice).
As king राम put the people's welfare first — रामराज्यम्, the ideal of righteous rule.
The verse रामो विग्रहवान् धर्मः calls Rama 'righteousness personified'.

sections.heading: Verses and sandhi
bullets: Four public-domain श्लोकाः praise Rama; 'राम राजमणिः…' shows राम in all eight cases.
दीर्घ-सन्धि: राज्य + अभिषेकः = राज्याभिषेकः (अ+अ=आ); वध + अनन्तरम् = वधानन्तरम्.
यण्-सन्धि: प्रति + आगमनम् = प्रत्यागमनम् (इ+आ = य्+आ).
सन्धि-विच्छेदः (splitting) is a key reading skill: रामान्नास्ति = रामात् + न + अस्ति.

sections.heading: Vibhakti, shabda-rupa and dhatu-rupa
bullets: The eight विभक्ति endings of राम: रामः, रामम्, रामेण, रामाय, रामात्, रामस्य, रामे, (हे) राम.
प्रथमा marks the subject (रामः अगच्छत्); द्वितीया the object (सीताम्); तृतीया 'by' (विमानेन).
शब्दरूप of a-stem राम runs through three numbers: रामः / रामौ / रामाः …
धातुरूप of गम् (present): गच्छति / गच्छतः / गच्छन्ति; past forms अगच्छत्, अभवत्, अकरोत्.

key_takeaways: अयोध्यां प्रत्यागमनम् retells how श्रीराम came home after fourteen years of वनवासः — the joy celebrated as दीपावली.
विभीषण's पुष्पकविमान carried राम, सीता and लक्ष्मण back through the sky to अयोध्या.
भरत ruled selflessly with राम's पादुके on the throne, showing भ्रातृप्रेम and त्यागः.
वसिष्ठ crowned राम king, beginning रामराज्यम् — the timeless symbol of just, compassionate rule.
The verse रामो विग्रहवान् धर्मः calls Rama 'dharma personified'; रामाय … नमः salutes him.
दीर्घ- and यण्-सन्धि join sounds (राज्य+अभिषेकः=राज्याभिषेकः); splitting them is सन्धि-विच्छेदः.
The word राम models the eight विभक्ति endings and the धातु गम् models present-tense धातुरूप.

glossary.definition: Return, coming back (प्रति + आगमनम्); here श्रीराम's return to अयोध्या after exile.
Dwelling in the forest; the fourteen-year exile of राम, सीता and लक्ष्मण.
The flying aerial car, given by विभीषण, on which राम returned to अयोध्या.
The pair of sandals; भरत placed राम's पादुके on the throne and ruled in his name.
Coronation; the consecration of राम as king, performed by the sage वसिष्ठ.
'The rule of Rama'; the ideal, righteous and prosperous kingdom in which all people are happy.
राम's brother who ruled अयोध्या as a humble ascetic-regent, keeping the throne for राम.
The devoted vanara who carried the news of राम's return to भरत at नन्दिग्राम.
Righteousness, duty, moral law; राम is called 'विग्रहवान् धर्मः', righteousness personified.
The doing of one's duty; राम kept his father's promise, honouring सत्यम् (truth).
The joining/merging of sounds where words meet, e.g. राज्य + अभिषेकः = राज्याभिषेकः.
The splitting of a joined form back into its parts, e.g. प्रत्यागमनम् = प्रति + आगमनम्.
A noun's case ending showing its role; राम has eight — रामः, रामम्, रामेण, रामाय, रामात्, रामस्य, रामे, (हे) राम.
The full declension of a noun through cases and numbers, e.g. राम: रामः / रामौ / रामाः.
The conjugation of a verb-root, e.g. गम् (to go) → गच्छति / गच्छतः / गच्छन्ति in the present.

worksheet.title: Worksheet — अयोध्यां प्रत्यागमनम् (NIOS Sanskrit 209, Chapter 7)
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Write Sanskrit words in Devanagari and give your explanations in English. Refer to the lesson and the verses where needed.

questions.question: For how many years did श्रीराम live in the forest, and with whom did he go?
questions.answer: श्रीराम lived in the forest for चतुर्दश वर्षाणि (fourteen years). His wife सीता and his brother लक्ष्मण went with him to keep his father दशरथ's promise.
questions.explanation: The exile lasted fourteen years; Sita and Lakshmana accompanied Rama.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English meaning) of each: प्रत्यागमनम्, विमानम्, पादुके, राज्याभिषेकः, प्रजाः.
questions.answer: प्रत्यागमनम् = return/coming back; विमानम् = aerial car (flying vehicle); पादुके = the pair of sandals; राज्याभिषेकः = coronation; प्रजाः = subjects/people.
questions.explanation: Key vocabulary from the lesson.

questions.question: How did भरत rule अयोध्या during राम's exile? What does this show about him?
questions.answer: भरत placed राम's पादुके (sandals) upon the सिंहासन (throne) and ruled as a humble तापस (ascetic) in राम's name, not as king himself. It shows his भ्रातृप्रेम (brotherly love), त्यागः (sacrifice) and humility.
questions.explanation: Bharata was a selfless regent, holding the throne only in trust for Rama.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद (split) of: (a) राज्याभिषेकः (b) प्रत्यागमनम्.
questions.answer: (a) राज्याभिषेकः = राज्य + अभिषेकः (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घ-सन्धि). (b) प्रत्यागमनम् = प्रति + आगमनम् (इ + आ = य् + आ, यण्-सन्धि).
questions.explanation: Splitting a joined form back into its words is सन्धि-विच्छेदः.

questions.question: State the विभक्ति (case) and meaning-role of each: रामः, सीताम्, विमानेन.
questions.answer: रामः = प्रथमा (nominative) → the subject/doer, 'Rama'. सीताम् = द्वितीया (accusative) → the object, 'Sita'. विमानेन = तृतीया (instrumental) → 'by/with the aerial car'.
questions.explanation: प्रथमा marks the subject, द्वितीया the object, तृतीया the means.

questions.question: Explain the idea of 'रामराज्यम्' and, using the verse 'रामो विग्रहवान् धर्मः साधुः सत्यपराक्रमः', describe how a good ruler should behave. How can students practise these values today?
questions.answer: रामराज्यम् means 'the rule of Rama' — an ideal kingdom in which the subjects (प्रजाः) live by धर्म (righteousness) and all are सुखिनः (happy) and निरामयाः (free from disease and sorrow). The verse 'रामो विग्रहवान् धर्मः साधुः सत्यपराक्रमः' calls Rama 'righteousness personified (विग्रहवान् धर्मः), noble (साधुः), of true valour (सत्यपराक्रमः)'. A good ruler should therefore be truthful, just, brave, and should place the welfare of the people above his own comfort — as Rama did. Students can practise these values by being honest, keeping their word, treating everyone fairly, protecting the weaker classmates, and serving their family and community selflessly. In this way each person builds a small 'Rama-rajya' of fairness and kindness around them.
questions.explanation: Define रामराज्यम्, connect it to the verse describing Rama as dharma, and give practical applications.

questions.question: Write three simple Sanskrit sentences (in Devanagari) about राम's return to अयोध्या, and give their English meanings.
questions.answer:
1. रामः चतुर्दश वर्षाणि वने अवसत्। (Rama lived in the forest for fourteen years.)
2. सः रावणं हत्वा अयोध्यां प्रत्यागच्छत्। (Having killed Ravana, he returned to Ayodhya.)
3. वसिष्ठः रामस्य राज्याभिषेकम् अकरोत्। (Vasishtha performed Rama's coronation.)
Together: Rama, after his exile and victory, came home and was crowned king of Ayodhya.
questions.explanation: Simple sentences using प्रथमा subjects and past-tense verbs (अवसत्, प्रत्यागच्छत्, अकरोत्) from the chapter vocabulary.

questions.question: Translate the verse: 'रामाय रामभद्राय रामचन्द्राय वेधसे । रघुनाथाय नाथाय सीतायाः पतये नमः ॥' and name the case in which the word 'राम' repeatedly appears.
questions.answer: Translation: Salutation to Rama, to the gracious Rama (रामभद्र), to Ramachandra, to the wise/creator (वेधस्); salutation to the lord of the Raghus (रघुनाथ), the protector (नाथ), the husband of Sita. The word राम appears again and again in the चतुर्थी (dative) case — रामाय, 'to Rama' — because it is a verse of salutation (नमः takes the dative).
questions.explanation: नमः governs the dative (चतुर्थी); hence रामाय, रामभद्राय, रामचन्द्राय.

questions.question: Why is the return of श्रीराम to अयोध्या celebrated as दीपावली?
questions.answer: When राम returned to अयोध्या after fourteen years of exile, the citizens rejoiced and lit rows of lamps (दीप) and decorated the city with flowers and festoons to welcome him. This joyful welcome with lamps is remembered every year as दीपावली, the 'festival of lamps'.
questions.explanation: Deepavali commemorates the lamp-lit welcome of Rama's homecoming.

questions.question: Give the धातुरूप (present tense, लट् लकार) of the verb गम् (गच्छ्) in the third person (प्रथम-पुरुष), all three numbers.
questions.answer: गच्छति (एकवचन — he/she goes), गच्छतः (द्विवचन — the two go), गच्छन्ति (बहुवचन — they go).
questions.explanation: गम् is a first-class root that takes the stem गच्छ- in the present tense.

questions.question: सन्धि: 'वध + अनन्तरम्' = ?
questions.explanation: अ + अ = आ (दीर्घ-सन्धि).

questions.question: सन्धि: 'राम + अयनम्' = ?
questions.explanation: अ + अ = आ; 'Ramayana' = the way/journey of Rama.

questions.question: सन्धि-विच्छेद: 'रामान्नास्ति' = ?
questions.explanation: त् + न = न्न (व्यञ्जन-सन्धि); न + अस्ति = नास्ति.

questions.question: In 'रामो विग्रहवान्', the form रामो comes from
questions.explanation: Visarga before a soft consonant → ओ (विसर्ग-सन्धि).

questions.question: Splitting a joined Sanskrit word back into its parts is called
questions.explanation: सन्धि-विच्छेद = the reverse of sandhi, i.e. splitting.

questions.question: In 'रामः अयोध्यां प्रत्यागच्छत्', the word 'रामः' is in which विभक्ति?
questions.explanation: रामः is the subject, hence प्रथमा (nominative).

questions.question: In 'रामः सीताम् अपश्यत्', the word 'सीताम्' is in which विभक्ति?
questions.explanation: सीताम् is the object, hence द्वितीया (accusative).

questions.question: 'रामाय नमः' — the word रामाय is in which विभक्ति?
questions.explanation: नमः governs the dative; रामाय = 'to Rama'.

questions.question: 'दशरथस्य पुत्रः' — the word दशरथस्य is in which विभक्ति?
questions.explanation: षष्ठी shows 'of', possession: 'of Dasharatha'.

questions.question: 'वने' (in 'वने अवसत्') is in which विभक्ति?
questions.explanation: सप्तमी shows place: 'in the forest'.

questions.question: The प्रथमा (nominative) plural of राम is
questions.explanation: प्रथमा बहुवचन of राम = रामाः.

questions.question: धातुरूप: the present-tense (लट्) third-person singular of गम् is
questions.explanation: गम् takes stem गच्छ-; गच्छति = 'he goes'.

questions.question: In 'रामो विग्रहवान् धर्मः', Rama is described as
questions.explanation: विग्रहवान् धर्मः = dharma having a (human) form.

questions.question: The verse 'राम राजमणिः सदा विजयते…' is specially useful for learning
questions.explanation: It displays राम in all eight cases (nominative to vocative).

questions.question: 'आपदामपहर्तारम्' describes Rama as the one who
questions.explanation: आपदाम् अपहर्तारम् = the remover of calamities.

questions.question: श्रीराम lived in the forest for fourteen years (चतुर्दश वर्षाणि).
questions.explanation: The exile lasted fourteen years.

questions.question: भरत placed राम's पादुके on the throne and ruled in his name.
questions.explanation: Bharata ruled as regent with the sandals on the throne.

questions.question: रावण gave the पुष्पकविमान to राम for the journey home.
questions.explanation: It was विभीषण, not Ravana, who gave the Pushpaka.

questions.question: रामराज्यम् stands for an ideal, righteous and prosperous rule.
questions.explanation: Rama-rajya is the symbol of just, compassionate governance.

questions.question: The sage वसिष्ठ performed राम's राज्याभिषेक (coronation).
questions.explanation: Vasishtha, the royal preceptor, crowned Rama.

questions.question: The word 'विमानम्' means a boat.
questions.explanation: विमानम् means an aerial car / flying vehicle, not a boat.

questions.question: 'प्रत्यागमनम्' splits as प्रति + आगमनम् (यण्-सन्धि).
questions.explanation: इ + आ = य् + आ gives प्रत्यागमनम्.

questions.question: भरत ruled अयोध्या out of greed for the throne.
questions.explanation: He ruled selflessly, keeping the throne in trust for Rama.

questions.question: राम's homecoming is celebrated every year as होली.
questions.explanation: It is celebrated as दीपावली (Deepavali), the festival of lamps.

questions.question: In 'रामः वनम् अगच्छत्', the word रामः is in the प्रथमा (nominative) case.
questions.explanation: रामः is the subject, hence nominative.

questions.question: श्रीरामः ______ वर्षाणि वने अवसत्।
questions.explanation: The exile lasted fourteen (चतुर्दश) years.

questions.question: रामः रावणं हत्वा ______ प्रत्यागच्छत्।
questions.explanation: Rama returned to Ayodhya (accusative अयोध्याम्).

questions.question: भरतः रामस्य ______ सिंहासने अस्थापयत्।
questions.explanation: Bharata placed the sandals (पादुके) on the throne.

questions.question: गुरुः ______ रामस्य राज्याभिषेकम् अकरोत्।
questions.explanation: The preceptor Vasishtha performed the coronation.

questions.question: रामस्य माता ______ आसीत्।
questions.explanation: Rama's mother was Kausalya.

questions.question: रामस्य पत्नी ______ आसीत्।
questions.explanation: Rama's wife was Sita.

questions.question: विभीषणः रामाय ______ विमानम् अयच्छत्।
questions.explanation: Vibhishana gave the Pushpaka (पुष्पकम्) aerial car.

questions.question: राज्य + अभिषेकः = ______।
questions.explanation: अ + अ = आ (दीर्घ-सन्धि).

questions.question: प्रति + आगमनम् = ______।
questions.explanation: इ + आ = य् + आ (यण्-सन्धि).

questions.question: गम् धातोः लट्लकारे प्रथमपुरुष-एकवचनम् ______।
questions.explanation: गम् → गच्छति (he goes).

questions.question: राम-शब्दस्य प्रथमा-एकवचनम् ______।
questions.explanation: The nominative singular of राम is रामः.

questions.question: रामस्य आदर्शराज्यं ______ इति प्रसिद्धम्।
questions.explanation: Rama's ideal kingdom is famous as रामराज्यम्.

questions.question: 'वनम्' इत्यस्य अर्थः ______ (in English).
questions.explanation: वनम् = forest.

questions.question: 'राक्षसः' इत्यस्य अर्थः ______ (in English).
questions.explanation: राक्षसः = demon.

questions.question: 'रामाय नमः' — अत्र 'रामाय' पदं ______ विभक्तौ अस्ति।
questions.explanation: नमः governs the dative (चतुर्थी).

questions.question: After defeating रावण, how did राम travel back to अयोध्या, and who gave him the means?
questions.answer: After killing Ravana, Rama travelled back through the sky (आकाशमार्गेण) on the पुष्पकविमान, the flying aerial car. विभीषण, Ravana's righteous brother, gave him this vehicle. Sita, Lakshmana, Sugriva, Hanuman, Vibhishana and the vanaras journeyed with him.
questions.explanation: Vibhishana gave the Pushpaka; Rama flew home with his companions.

questions.question: Whom did राम meet on the way home, and whom did he send ahead to भरत?
questions.answer: On the way Rama stopped at the आश्रम (hermitage) of the sage भरद्वाज at Prayaga, who welcomed them warmly. Rama then sent हनुमान् ahead to नन्दिग्राम to carry the good news of his return to भरत.
questions.explanation: Rama met sage Bharadwaja and sent Hanuman ahead to Bharata.

questions.question: Describe how भरत had governed अयोध्या during the fourteen years of राम's exile.
questions.answer: भरत refused to sit on the throne himself. He placed राम's पादुके (sandals) upon the सिंहासन and ruled only as their servant, living simply in the dress of a तापस (ascetic) at नन्दिग्राम. Thus he governed in Rama's name, keeping the kingdom in trust for his elder brother.
questions.explanation: Bharata ruled as a humble ascetic-regent with Rama's sandals on the throne.

questions.question: What was the role of the sage वसिष्ठ in this episode?
questions.answer: वसिष्ठ was the royal preceptor (गुरु) of the family. He performed राम's राज्याभिषेक (coronation) at an auspicious hour (शुभे मुहूर्ते), formally making Rama the king of Ayodhya.
questions.explanation: Vasishtha crowned Rama king at an auspicious time.

questions.question: How did माता कौसल्या react on seeing राम return?
questions.answer: माता कौसल्या, राम's mother, was overwhelmed with happiness. Seeing her son after fourteen years, she wept with joy (हर्षेण अरोदीत्) and embraced him.
questions.explanation: Kausalya wept with joy at seeing her son again.

questions.question: What is meant by राज्याभिषेकः, and why was it important here?
questions.answer: राज्याभिषेकः (राज्य + अभिषेकः) means the coronation or consecration of a king. Here it marked the moment when राम, after exile and victory, was formally enthroned as king of अयोध्या by वसिष्ठ, beginning the era of रामराज्यम् (righteous rule).
questions.explanation: Coronation of Rama as king, beginning Rama-rajya.

questions.question: Explain the idea of रामराज्यम् in two or three sentences.
questions.answer: रामराज्यम् means 'the rule of Rama'. It describes an ideal kingdom in which the subjects (प्रजाः) live by धर्म (righteousness) and everyone is सुखी (happy) and निरामय (free from disease and sorrow). It has become India's timeless symbol of just and compassionate governance.
questions.explanation: Rama-rajya is the ideal of righteous, prosperous, compassionate rule.

questions.question: Why is राम's return connected with the festival of दीपावली?
questions.answer: When राम returned to अयोध्या, the joyful citizens lit rows of lamps (दीप) and decorated the city with flowers and festoons to welcome him. This lamp-lit welcome is remembered every year as दीपावली, the festival of lamps.
questions.explanation: Deepavali commemorates the lamp-lit welcome of Rama's homecoming.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English meaning) of: वनवासः, प्रजाः, धर्मः, आश्रमः.
questions.answer: वनवासः = dwelling in the forest / exile; प्रजाः = subjects / people; धर्मः = righteousness / duty; आश्रमः = hermitage.
questions.explanation: Core vocabulary from the lesson.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English meaning) of: अपालयत्, अशोभयन्, प्रणम्य, अर्पयत्.
questions.answer: अपालयत् = (he) ruled / protected; अशोभयन् = (they) adorned / decorated; प्रणम्य = having bowed; अर्पयत् = (he) offered / gave back.
questions.explanation: Verb-forms and gerund from the narrative.

questions.question: What moral do we learn from भरत's conduct during राम's exile?
questions.answer: भरत teaches selfless love and sacrifice. Though he could have enjoyed the throne, he refused it, ruling humbly in his brother's name and returning the kingdom joyfully. His conduct shows भ्रातृप्रेम (brotherly love), त्यागः (sacrifice) and respect for dharma over personal gain.
questions.explanation: Bharata models brotherly love, sacrifice and selflessness.

questions.question: Which values does the whole homecoming episode teach? Name at least three.
questions.answer: The episode teaches: (1) सत्यम् and कर्तव्यपालनम् — Rama kept his father's promise and completed the exile; (2) भ्रातृप्रेम and त्यागः — Bharata's selfless regency; (3) धर्मराज्यम् / रामराज्यम् — righteous, people-first governance. Together they show that truth, duty and love lead to lasting happiness.
questions.explanation: Truth, duty, brotherly love, sacrifice and righteous rule.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद (split) of: (a) रामायणम् (b) वधानन्तरम्.
questions.answer: (a) रामायणम् = राम + अयनम् (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घ-सन्धि). (b) वधानन्तरम् = वध + अनन्तरम् (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घ-सन्धि).
questions.explanation: Both are examples of दीर्घ-सन्धि (like vowels merging into a long vowel).

questions.question: Join by सन्धि: (a) राज्य + अभिषेकः (b) प्रति + आगमनम्. Name the sandhi.
questions.answer: (a) राज्य + अभिषेकः = राज्याभिषेकः (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घ-सन्धि). (b) प्रति + आगमनम् = प्रत्यागमनम् (इ + आ = य् + आ, यण्-सन्धि).
questions.explanation: One दीर्घ-सन्धि and one यण्-सन्धि.

questions.question: State the विभक्ति (case) and meaning-role of: रामेण, वने, रामस्य.
questions.answer: रामेण = तृतीया (instrumental) → 'by/with Rama'. वने = सप्तमी (locative) → 'in the forest'. रामस्य = षष्ठी (genitive) → 'of Rama'.
questions.explanation: तृतीया = means, सप्तमी = place, षष्ठी = possession.

questions.question: Give the धातुरूप (present tense) of गम् in the second person (मध्यम-पुरुष), all three numbers.
questions.answer: गच्छसि (एकवचन — you go), गच्छथः (द्विवचन — you two go), गच्छथ (बहुवचन — you all go).
questions.explanation: Second-person present forms of गम् (stem गच्छ-).

questions.question: Translate: 'रामो विग्रहवान् धर्मः साधुः सत्यपराक्रमः।'
questions.answer: Rama is righteousness personified (विग्रहवान् धर्मः), noble/virtuous (साधुः), and of true valour (सत्यपराक्रमः). The verse praises Rama as dharma taken human form.
questions.explanation: The line calls Rama dharma embodied, virtuous and truly valiant.

questions.question: Translate: 'आपदामपहर्तारं दातारं सर्वसम्पदाम्।' and say whom it praises.
questions.answer: Translation: 'Him who removes all calamities (आपदाम् अपहर्तारम्), the giver of every prosperity (दातारं सर्वसम्पदाम्)…'. It praises श्रीराम, from the रामरक्षास्तोत्रम्.
questions.explanation: It praises Sri Rama as remover of troubles and giver of prosperity.

questions.question: Why did श्रीराम go to the forest for fourteen years?
questions.answer: Rama went to the forest to keep his father दशरथ's promise (पितुः वचनं पालयितुम्). Honouring his father's word, he accepted the exile without complaint, upholding सत्यम् (truth) and कर्तव्य (duty).
questions.explanation: To keep his father's promise — an act of truth and duty.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English meaning) of: सिंहासनम्, तोरणैः, निरामयाः, हर्षेण.
questions.answer: सिंहासनम् = throne; तोरणैः = with festoons / decorative arches; निरामयाः = free from disease; हर्षेण = with joy.
questions.explanation: Vocabulary of the welcome and the happy kingdom.

questions.question: What did भरत do with the पादुके when राम returned?
questions.answer: When राम returned, भरत bowed to him (प्रणम्य), took राम's पादुके down from the throne, and reverently gave them back to राम (पादुके तस्मै अर्पयत्), joyfully handing over the kingdom to its rightful king.
questions.explanation: Bharata bowed and returned the sandals to Rama.

questions.question: Translate into simple English: 'रामः रावणं हत्वा सीतया सह अयोध्यां प्रत्यागच्छत्।'
questions.answer: Rama, having killed Ravana (रावणं हत्वा), returned to Ayodhya (अयोध्यां प्रत्यागच्छत्) together with Sita (सीतया सह). Here रावणम् is the object, सीतया 'with Sita' is instrumental, and अयोध्याम् is the goal of the motion.
questions.explanation: The sentence: after killing Ravana, Rama returned to Ayodhya with Sita.

questions.question: In your own words (in English), narrate the story of श्रीराम's return to अयोध्या from the killing of रावण to the coronation.
questions.answer: After fourteen years of exile and the great war in Lanka, Rama killed the demon Ravana and freed Sita. Wishing to return home, he accepted the flying chariot पुष्पकविमान from Vibhishana and set out through the sky with Sita, Lakshmana, Sugriva, Hanuman, Vibhishana and the vanaras. On the way they rested at sage Bharadwaja's hermitage at Prayaga. Rama then sent Hanuman ahead to Nandigrama to tell Bharata the good news. Bharata, who for fourteen years had ruled as a humble ascetic with Rama's sandals on the throne, rushed out overjoyed to meet him. When Rama entered Ayodhya, the citizens lit lamps and decorated the city; mother Kausalya wept with joy, and Bharata returned the sandals. The sage Vasishtha then crowned Rama king at an auspicious hour, and Rama's righteous rule — Rama-rajya — began, in which all the people lived happily and without suffering.
questions.explanation: A full retelling: Ravana's death, the Pushpaka flight, Bharadwaja, Hanuman's message, Bharata's regency, the joyful reunion and the coronation.

questions.question: Explain the significance of राम's राज्याभिषेकः and the meaning of रामराज्यम्. Why is it remembered even today?
questions.answer: राम's राज्याभिषेकः (coronation), performed by वसिष्ठ, was the joyful climax of the whole Ramayana: after exile, war and long separation, dharma was restored and the rightful king took his throne. It began रामराज्यम् — 'the rule of Rama' — an ideal kingdom in which the प्रजाः (subjects) lived by धर्म and all were सुखिनः (happy) and निरामयाः (free from disease and sorrow). Rama ruled not for his own pleasure but for the welfare of the people, with truth, justice and compassion. This is why रामराज्यम् is remembered even today as India's timeless symbol of good and fair governance — a standard against which just rule is measured.
questions.explanation: The coronation restores dharma; Rama-rajya = ideal, people-first righteous rule, still a symbol of good governance.

questions.question: Analyse the values shown by राम and भरत in this episode, and explain how a student can apply them in daily life.
questions.answer: राम shows सत्यम् (truth) and कर्तव्यपालनम् (duty): he kept his father's promise and completed the full exile without resentment, and as king he put the people's welfare first. भरत shows भ्रातृप्रेम (brotherly love), त्यागः (sacrifice) and humility: he refused the throne, ruled selflessly in his brother's name, and joyfully returned the kingdom. Together they teach that dharma matters more than personal comfort or power. A student can apply these values by keeping promises, doing homework and duties honestly, respecting elders, sharing with and helping siblings and friends, not being greedy for position, and treating everyone fairly. In this way each person creates a small 'Rama-rajya' of honesty and kindness around them.
questions.explanation: Rama: truth and duty; Bharata: love and sacrifice. Applications: honesty, promise-keeping, fairness, humility, service.

questions.question: Read the verse 'राम राजमणिः सदा विजयते रामं रमेशं भजे…'. Translate it and explain why it is useful for learning the eight विभक्ति of राम.
questions.answer: Translation: Rama, the jewel of kings (राजमणिः), is ever victorious; I worship Rama (रामम्), the lord of Lakshmi. By Rama (रामेण) the demon army was struck down; to that Rama (रामाय) my salutation. There is no higher refuge than Rama (रामात्); I am the servant of Rama (रामस्य); may my mind ever be absorbed in Rama (रामे); O Rama (राम), uplift me. The verse is famous because it uses the single word 'राम' once in each of the eight cases — प्रथमा (रामः/राजमणिः), द्वितीया (रामम्), तृतीया (रामेण), चतुर्थी (रामाय), पञ्चमी (रामात्), षष्ठी (रामस्य), सप्तमी (रामे) and सम्बोधन (हे राम) — so by memorising one beautiful verse a student learns the whole शब्दरूप of an a-stem noun.
questions.explanation: Translate the all-cases verse and show how it models प्रथमा–सम्बोधन of राम.

questions.question: Write a character sketch of भरत based on this episode.
questions.answer: भरत appears in this episode as a model of selflessness and devotion. Deeply attached to his elder brother राम, he could not bear to rule in Rama's place. Instead he placed राम's पादुके on the throne and governed अयोध्या only as their servant, living austerely like a तापस (ascetic) at नन्दिग्राम for fourteen years. He kept the kingdom safe and just, waiting faithfully for Rama's return. On hearing the news from हनुमान्, his eyes filled with tears of joy; he ran to meet Rama, bowed humbly, and gladly returned the sandals and the kingdom. भरत thus embodies भ्रातृप्रेम (brotherly love), त्यागः (sacrifice), humility, patience and unshakable devotion to dharma.
questions.explanation: Bharata: selfless, devoted, humble, patient regent who holds the throne in trust for Rama.

questions.question: Write the शब्दरूप of राम (masculine a-stem) in the singular (एकवचन) for all eight cases, with the English meaning of each.
questions.answer: प्रथमा: रामः (Rama — subject); द्वितीया: रामम् (Rama — object, 'Rama'); तृतीया: रामेण ('by/with Rama'); चतुर्थी: रामाय ('to/for Rama'); पञ्चमी: रामात् ('from/than Rama'); षष्ठी: रामस्य ('of Rama'); सप्तमी: रामे ('in/on Rama'); सम्बोधन: (हे) राम ('O Rama'). These eight forms are exactly the ones illustrated in the verse 'राम राजमणिः…'.
questions.explanation: The eight singular case-forms of राम with their roles.

questions.question: Explain सन्धि with four examples taken from this lesson, naming the type of each.
questions.answer: सन्धि is the joining/merging of sounds where two words meet. Examples from the lesson: (1) राज्य + अभिषेकः = राज्याभिषेकः — अ + अ = आ, दीर्घ-सन्धि. (2) वध + अनन्तरम् = वधानन्तरम् — अ + अ = आ, दीर्घ-सन्धि. (3) प्रति + आगमनम् = प्रत्यागमनम् — इ + आ = य् + आ, यण्-सन्धि. (4) रामः + विग्रहवान् = रामो विग्रहवान् — visarga before a soft sound → ओ, विसर्ग-सन्धि. Splitting such a joined form back into its parts is called सन्धि-विच्छेदः, a key reading skill.
questions.explanation: Four worked examples: two दीर्घ, one यण्, one विसर्ग sandhi, plus the idea of सन्धि-विच्छेद.

questions.question: Write a short paragraph of four simple Sanskrit sentences (in Devanagari) describing रामराज्यम्, and give the English meaning of each.
questions.answer:
1. रामः अयोध्यायाः राजा अभवत्। (Rama became the king of Ayodhya.)
2. तस्य राज्ये सर्वे जनाः सुखिनः आसन्। (In his kingdom all the people were happy.)
3. प्रजाः धर्मेण जीवन्ति स्म। (The subjects lived by righteousness.)
4. एतत् राज्यं 'रामराज्यम्' इति प्रसिद्धम्। (This kingdom is famous as 'Rama-rajya'.)
Together these sentences describe Rama-rajya as a happy, righteous and celebrated kingdom.
questions.explanation: Four correct simple sentences with प्रथमा subjects and past/present verbs describing Rama-rajya.

questions.question: निम्नलिखितं गद्यांशं पठित्वा प्रश्नस्य उत्तरं लिखत — 'रावणस्य वधानन्तरं रामः सीतया लक्ष्मणेन च सह अयोध्यां प्रत्यागन्तुम् ऐच्छत्। विभीषणः रामाय पुष्पकं विमानम् अयच्छत्। तेन विमानेन ते आकाशमार्गेण प्रस्थिताः।' प्रश्नः: राम कैसे और किसके साथ अयोध्या लौटे? (How and with whom did Rama return to Ayodhya?)
questions.answer: According to the passage, after the killing of Ravana Rama wished to return to Ayodhya. Vibhishana (विभीषणः) gave him the पुष्पकविमान (aerial car), and by that vehicle Rama set out through the sky-path (आकाशमार्गेण), together with Sita (सीता) and Lakshmana (लक्ष्मण) — and, as the lesson adds, Sugriva, Hanuman, Vibhishana and the vanaras.
questions.explanation: The passage states Rama returned by air on the Pushpaka, given by Vibhishana, with Sita and Lakshmana.

questions.question: गद्यांशं पठत — 'भरतः चतुर्दश वर्षाणि रामस्य पादुके सिंहासने स्थापयित्वा तापसवेषेण राज्यम् अपालयत्। समाचारं श्रुत्वा भरतस्य नेत्रे आनन्दाश्रुभिः पूर्णे अभवताम्।' प्रश्नः: भरत ने राज्य कैसे चलाया और समाचार सुनकर उसकी क्या दशा हुई? (How did Bharata run the kingdom, and how did he react to the news?)
questions.answer: The passage says that for fourteen years Bharata ruled by placing Rama's पादुके (sandals) on the throne and living in the dress of a तापस (ascetic) — that is, humbly and selflessly in Rama's name. When he heard the news of Rama's return, his two eyes (नेत्रे) filled with tears of joy (आनन्दाश्रुभिः).
questions.explanation: Bharata ruled as an ascetic-regent with the sandals on the throne; the news filled his eyes with tears of joy.

questions.question: गद्यांशं पठत — 'वसिष्ठः शुभे मुहूर्ते रामस्य राज्याभिषेकम् अकरोत्। तस्य शासने प्रजाः धर्मेण जीवन्ति स्म, सर्वे च सुखिनः निरामयाः च आसन्।' प्रश्नः: इस अंश से रामराज्य की कौन-कौन सी विशेषताएँ पता चलती हैं? (What features of Rama-rajya does this passage reveal?)
questions.answer: The passage reveals several features of रामराज्यम्: (1) Rama was properly consecrated as king by वसिष्ठ at an auspicious hour, so the rule was legitimate and dharmic; (2) under his शासन (rule) the प्रजाः (subjects) lived by धर्म (righteousness); (3) all people were सुखिनः (happy) and निरामयाः (free from disease and sorrow). Thus Rama-rajya is shown as a righteous, healthy, prosperous and happy kingdom.
questions.explanation: Features: righteous coronation, subjects living by dharma, everyone happy and free from disease.

questions.question: श्लोकं पठत — 'रामो विग्रहवान् धर्मः साधुः सत्यपराक्रमः। राजा सर्वस्य लोकस्य देवानामिव वासवः॥' प्रश्नः: इस श्लोक में राम का वर्णन किस प्रकार किया गया है? (How is Rama described in this verse?)
questions.answer: In this verse Rama is described as धर्मः विग्रहवान् — righteousness personified, dharma taken human form; as साधुः — noble and virtuous; and as सत्यपराक्रमः — one of true valour. He is called fit to be the राजा (king) of the whole world (सर्वस्य लोकस्य), just as वासव (Indra) is king of the gods (देवानाम्). The verse thus glorifies Rama as the ideal, righteous ruler.
questions.explanation: Rama = dharma embodied, noble, truly valiant, fit king of all the world like Indra of the gods.

questions.question: गद्यांशं पठत — 'रामः पितुः वचनं पालयितुम् चतुर्दश वर्षाणि वनम् अगच्छत्। भरतः राज्यलोभं त्यक्त्वा रामस्य पादुके पूजयन् राज्यम् अपालयत्।' प्रश्नः: इस अंश से राम और भरत के कौन से गुण प्रकट होते हैं? इन गुणों को हम कैसे अपना सकते हैं? (What virtues of Rama and Bharata appear here, and how can we adopt them?)
questions.answer: The passage shows Rama's सत्यम् and कर्तव्यपालनम् — he went to the forest for fourteen years only to keep his father's word — and Bharata's त्यागः and भ्रातृप्रेम — he gave up the greed for the throne (राज्यलोभं त्यक्त्वा) and ruled while honouring Rama's sandals. We can adopt these virtues by keeping our promises, doing our duties honestly, respecting elders, and being generous and unselfish with brothers, sisters and friends rather than greedy for position.
questions.explanation: Virtues: Rama's truth/duty and Bharata's sacrifice/brotherly love; adopt via honesty, duty and unselfishness.

questions.question: गद्यांशं पठत — 'मार्गे ते प्रयागे भरद्वाजस्य आश्रमम् अगच्छन्। ऋषिः तान् सस्नेहम् अपूजयत्। ततः रामः हनूमन्तं भरतस्य समीपं प्रैषयत्।' प्रश्नः: राम मार्ग में किसके आश्रम गए और उन्होंने किसे भरत के पास भेजा? (Whose hermitage did Rama visit on the way, and whom did he send to Bharata?)
questions.answer: According to the passage, on the way Rama and his companions went to the आश्रम (hermitage) of the sage भरद्वाज at Prayaga, where the sage honoured them affectionately. Then Rama sent हनुमान् (Hanuman) to Bharata to carry the news of his return.
questions.explanation: Rama visited Bharadwaja's hermitage at Prayaga and sent Hanuman to Bharata.

questions.question: श्लोकं पठत — 'रामाय रामभद्राय रामचन्द्राय वेधसे। रघुनाथाय नाथाय सीतायाः पतये नमः॥' प्रश्नः: इस श्लोक का भाव लिखत तथा 'राम' शब्द किस विभक्ति में बार-बार आया है? (Give the sense of this verse and name the case in which 'राम' repeatedly appears.)
questions.answer: Sense: 'Salutation (नमः) to Rama, to the gracious Rama (रामभद्र), to Ramachandra, to the wise/creator (वेधस्); to the lord of the Raghus (रघुनाथ), to the protector (नाथ), to the husband of Sita.' The word राम appears again and again in the चतुर्थी (dative) case — रामाय, रामभद्राय, रामचन्द्राय — because नमः ('salutation') is used with the dative.
questions.explanation: A verse of salutation to Rama; राम is repeatedly in the dative (चतुर्थी) because नमः takes the dative.

questions.question: गद्यांशं पठत — 'रामे अयोध्यां प्रविष्टे सति सर्वे नागरिकाः प्रसन्नाः अभवन्। जनाः गृहाणि दीपैः पुष्पैः तोरणैः च अशोभयन्।' प्रश्नः: रेखांकित शब्दों के अर्थ लिखत — नागरिकाः, दीपैः, अशोभयन्। (Give the meanings of the words: नागरिकाः, दीपैः, अशोभयन्.)
questions.answer: नागरिकाः = the citizens / townspeople; दीपैः = with lamps (instrumental plural of दीप); अशोभयन् = (they) adorned / decorated. The passage means: when Rama entered Ayodhya, all the citizens became happy and the people decorated their houses with lamps, flowers and festoons.
questions.explanation: नागरिकाः = citizens; दीपैः = with lamps; अशोभयन् = decorated.

questions.question: वाक्यं पठत — 'रामः पुष्पकविमानेन अयोध्यां अगच्छत्।' प्रश्नः: इस वाक्य में 'रामः', 'पुष्पकविमानेन' तथा 'अयोध्याम्' किस-किस विभक्ति में हैं? (In which cases are the words रामः, पुष्पकविमानेन and अयोध्याम्?)
questions.answer: रामः = प्रथमा (nominative) — the subject/doer, 'Rama'. पुष्पकविमानेन = तृतीया (instrumental) — 'by the Pushpaka aerial car', showing the means. अयोध्याम् = द्वितीया (accusative) — the goal/object of motion, 'to Ayodhya'. The verb अगच्छत् is गम् in the past tense, 'went'.
questions.explanation: रामः nominative, पुष्पकविमानेन instrumental (means), अयोध्याम् accusative (goal of motion).

questions.question: वाक्यं पठत — 'रावणस्य वधानन्तरं रामः अयोध्यां प्रत्यागच्छत्।' प्रश्नः: 'वधानन्तरम्' तथा 'प्रत्यागच्छत्' में जो सन्धियाँ हैं उनका विच्छेद करत। (Split the sandhis found in वधानन्तरम् and प्रत्यागच्छत्.)
questions.answer: वधानन्तरम् = वध + अनन्तरम् (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घ-सन्धि), meaning 'after the killing'. प्रत्यागच्छत् = प्रति + आगच्छत् (इ + आ = य् + आ, यण्-सन्धि), meaning '(he) came back / returned'. Both show how vowels combine when words meet, and splitting them is सन्धि-विच्छेदः.
questions.explanation: वधानन्तरम् = वध + अनन्तरम् (दीर्घ); प्रत्यागच्छत् = प्रति + आगच्छत् (यण्).
